questions.question: Find the work done (in kJ) if a force of 750 N pushes a cart of mass 30 kg by 16 m.
questions.solution:
__CONCEPT:__

__
 
• Work is said to be done by a force when the body is displaced actually through some distance in the direction of the applied force.
 
• Since the body is being displaced in the direction of F, therefore work done by the force in displacing the body through a distance s is given by

W = vec F · vec s

Or, W = Fs cos θ

 
• Thus work done by a force is equal to the scalar or dot product of the force and the displacement of the body.

**CALCULATION**__:

Given that:

*⇒ *Force, F = 750 N

*⇒ *displacement, s = 16 m

*⇒ *Work done, w = Fs Cos θ 

Here θ is zero degree so Cos θ = 1

*⇒ W* = 750 × 16

*⇒ W* = 12000 J

To convert Joule into Kilo Joule divide by 1000

*⇒ *w = 12000 / 1000

*⇒ ***Work done, W = 12 KJ**

*⇒ ****__Note:__***** **1 Joule = 0.001 Kilo Joule

The astronaut weighs 90 kgf on Earth. This means that the astronaut weighs 90 x 10 = 900 N (since under Earth's gravity 1kgf = 1N 10 m/s²).

 

On the moon, the acceleration due to gravity is 1/6 of that on Earth, so the astronaut's weight will be 1/6 of his weight on Earth.

 

This gives us 1/6 × 900 N = 150 N

 

So, the correct answer is: 150 N.

 

**An astronaut who weighs 90 kg on Earth will weigh 150 N on the moon**

__**Concept:**__

**Mechanical advantage:**

__
 
• It is a number that tells us how many times a simple machine multiplies the effort force. 
 
• is defined as the **ratio of output force to input force.**
 
• The mechanical advantage of a machine gives its efficiency. 
 
• Formula, MA=(F₀)/(F_i), where, F₀ = output force, Fᵢ = input force
 
• It is a unitless and dimensionless quantity.

**Efficiency:**

 
• The efficiency of a machine is the **ratio of the work done on the load by the machine to the work done on the machine by the effort.**
 
• Thus, it is the ratio of useful work done by the machine output to the work done by the machine input.
 
• It is represented by the Greek symbol η.
 
• Formula, efficiency, eta=(mechanical advantage)/(velocity ratio)

Velocity ratio:

 
• The ratio of the distance moved by the point at which the effort is applied in a simple machine to the distance moved by the point at which the load is applied at the same time.
 
• Formula, velocity ratio=(distance moved by effort)/(distance moved by load)
 
• In the case of an ideal (frictionless and weightless) machine, velocity ratio = mechanical advantage.

**Calculation:**__

Given: mechanical advantage, MA = 2.5, length of load lift, LR = 2.5 m, length of effort, LE = 10 m

Velocity ratio, v=(10)/(2.5)=4

Efficiency, eta=(mechanical advantage)/(velocity ratio)

eta=(2.5)/(4)=0.625

**In percentage, the efficiency is 62.50 %.**

• The act or science of measuring the changes in the state variables of a body in order to calculate the heat transfer associated with changes in its states, such as physical changes or phase transitions under specific conditions, is known as calorimetry.
 
• Calorimetry is performed with the help of a calorimeter.

**Calorimetry Principle:**

 
• When two bodies of different temperatures are placed in physical contact with each other, the heat is transferred from the body with a higher temperature to the body with a lower temperature until thermal equilibrium is attained between them.
 
• The body at a higher temperature releases heat while the body at a lower temperature absorbs heat.
 
• **The principle of calorimetry indicates the law of conservation energy,** i.e. the total heat lost by the hot body is equal to the total heat gained by the cold body.
 
• **Heat Lost = Heat Gained**
 
• 
 
**The heat transfer in a system is calculated using the formula, Q = mcΔT**, Where Q = the measure of heat transfer, m = the mass of the body, c = the specific heat of the body, Δt = the change in the temperature

 
 
• 
 
The final temperature of the mixture is given as, T=(m₁s₁T₁+m₂s₂T₂)/(m₁s₁+m₂s₂), where T represents temperature, m represents mass and the s represents the specific heat

 

**Calculation:**__

Given: Temperatures, T₁ = 90 ºC, T₂ = 10 ºC, Masses, m₁ = 0.5 litre = 0.5 kg, m₂ = 3.5 litre = 3.5 kg

The final equilibrium temperature of the mixture can be calculated as,

T=(m₁s₁T₁+m₂s₂T₂)/(m₁s₁+m₂s₂)

Here, s₁ = s₂ = s (specific heat)

T=(m₁T₁+m₂T₂)/(m₁+m₂)

T=(0.5times 90+ 3.5times 10)/(0.5+3.5)

T = 20 ºC

**Hence, the final equilibrium temperature is 20 ºC.**

questions.question: What happens to the engine when the fan belt is too tight?
questions.solution:
__**Explanation:**__

**Engine Cooling System:**

 
• Combustion of fuel inside a cylinder develops a very high temperature (Approx. 2200° C).
 
• At this temperature, the engine parts will expand and tend to seize.
 
• Similarly, the lubricating oil will lose its property.
 
• Therefore it is necessary to keep the engine temperature to operating limits.
 
• This is done by the cooling system.

Types of cooling systems:

 
• Direct cooling - air cooling
 
• Indirect cooling - water cooling

**Water cooling:**

Two types of water cooling systems are used:

 
• Thermo-siphon system
 
• Forced circulation system

**Pump circulation system (Forced feed/circulation system):**

 
• In this system, water is circulated by a pump (3).
 
• The pump is driven by a fan belt (5) which is connected to the crankshaft pulley.
 
• **When the fan belt is too tight, the water pump stops working.**
 
• The circulation depends upon the engine speed.
 
• More water is circulated at higher engine speed.
 
• The water absorbs heat from the engine and flows to the radiator’s (2) top tank.
 
• Water from the top tank of the radiator (2) flows down to the bottom tank.
 
• The fan (4) draws the air through the radiator’s fins and cools the hot water.
 
• Cold water from the bottom tank is again pumped to the engine and the cycle is repeated.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/54e3fb5914abc6a9529934d75278aa638583acdffffe8f5c8c4fb0e8c1cd00e7.png] 

**Water pump:**

 
• The centrifugal-type water pump is used in engines.
 
• It is mounted on the front side of the cylinder block or head.
 
• The water pump is driven by the crankshaft pulley through the fan belt.
 
• The impeller is mounted on one end of the water pump shaft.
 
• The shaft is fitted in the pump housing with bearings.
 
• A water seal is provided in the pump to prevent leakage of water and to prevent water from entering into the bearings.
 
• When the impeller rotates it draws water from the lower tank of the radiator, and pumps water to the engine block, by centrifugal force under pressure.
 
• The fan is mounted on the water pump pulley.

questions.question: The distance between the centerlines of the main journal and the crank shaft pin is called:

Basic technical terms used in relation to engines:

Throw:

 
• **It is the distance between the centre of the crank pin to the centre of the main journal.**
 
• The piston stroke is double the throw.

T.D.C. (Top dead centre):

 
• It is the position of the piston at the top of a cylinder, where the piston changes its direction of motion from the top to the bottom.

B.D.C. (Bottom dead centre):

 
• It is the position of the piston at the bottom of the cylinder where the piston changes its direction of motion from the bottom to the top.

Stroke:

 
• The distance travelled by the piston from TDC to BDC or BDC to TDC.

Cycle:

 
• A set of operations performed in sequence by the motion of the piston in an engine to produce power.

Swept volume (VS):

 
• Displacement volume of a piston.

Clearance volume (VC):

 
• The volume of the space above the piston when it is at TDC.
 
• The space (volume) between the cylinder head and the piston head, when the piston is at TDC is called clearance volume.

Compression ratio (CR):

 
• The ratio of compression volumes before the stroke and after.
 
• CR = (V_S~+~V_C)/(V_C)

Where, VS = Swept volume, VC = Clearance volume, VS + VC = Total volume at BDC

Power:

 
• Power is the rate at which work is done in a specific time.

Horsepower (HP):

 
• It is the measurement of power in SAE. One hp is the power required to lift a load of 33000 lbs, through one foot in one minute or 4500 kg through one meter in one minute (in metric system)

Thermal efficiency:

 
• It is the ratio of work output to the fuel energy burnt in the engine. This relationship is expressed in percentage.

Brake horsepower (BHP):

 
• It is the power output of an engine, available at the flywheel.

BHP~=~(2pi NT)/(4500) 

Where, N is r.p.m of the crankshaft, and T is the torque produced.

Indicated horsepower (IHP):

 
• It is the power developed in the engine cylinder.

IHP~=~(PLAN)/(4500)~times~k 

Where Pm is the mean effective pressure in kg/cm2

 
• L is length of stroke in metres
 
• A is the area of the piston in cm2
 
• N is the No. of power strokes per minute
 
• k is the No. of cylinders.

Frictional horsepower:

 
• It is the horsepower lost in the engine due to friction.

FHP = IHP – BHP

Mechanical efficiency:

 
• It is the ratio of power delivered (BHP) and the power available in the engine (IHP). It is expressed in percentage.

Volumetric efficiency:

 
• It is the ratio between the air drawn in the cylinder during the suction stroke and the volume of the cylinder.

Firing order:

 
• The firing order is the sequence in which the power stroke takes place in each cylinder in a multi-cylinder engine.

• Drills are made from high-speed steel.

• The flutes provide a correct cutting angle which provides an escape path for the chips.
 
• It carries the coolant to the cutting edge during drilling.
 
• The portions left between the flutes are called lands.
 
• The size of a drill is determined and governed by the diameter of the land.

Four-stroke diesel engine:

 
• To produce power in a four-stroke engine the following operations take place in the sequence given below.

Suction stroke:

 
• The piston moves from TDC to BDC.
 
• A vacuum is created inside the cylinder.
 
• The inlet valve opens while the exhaust valve remains closed.
 
• The air enters the cylinder.

Compression stroke:

 
• The inlet valve closes.
 
• The exhaust valve remains closed.
 
• The piston moves from BDC to TDC.
 
• **The air is compressed.**
 
• The pressure and temperature rise.

Power stroke:

 
• The fuel is injected in the compressed air and the mixture is ignited and pressure develops inside the cylinder.
 
• The gas expands and the piston is forced down from TDC to BDC.
 
• Both valves remain closed. Power is supplied to the flywheel.

Exhaust stroke:

 
• The inlet valve remains in the closed position.
 
• The exhaust valve opens, and the piston moves from BDC to TDC due to the energy stored in the flywheel.
 
• The burnt gases inside the cylinder go out through the exhaust valves.
 
• At the end of the stroke, the exhaust valve closes.

• Vane type

• It consists of an impeller that rotates at a very high speed, about 10,000 r.p.m.

• The working action of such a supercharger is just like a gear pump so that the mixture at the outlet side is at high pressure.

**Vane-type supercharger:**

 
• It consists of a drum on which a number of vanes are mounted in such a manner that they can slide in or out against some spring force so that all the times they are in contact with the inner surface of the supercharger body.
 
• The space between the body and the drum goes on decreasing from the inlet to the outlet side.
 
• Thus, the air-fuel mixture entrapped between any two vanes at the inlet goes on decreasing in volume and increasing in pressure as it reaches the outlet.

questions.question: The movement of piston from TDC to BDC is called:
questions.solution:
__Explanation:__

Basic technical terms used in relation to engines:

T.D.C. (Top dead centre):

 
• It is the position of the piston at the top of a cylinder, where the piston changes its direction of motion from the top to the bottom.

B.D.C. (Bottom dead centre):

 
• It is the position of the piston at the bottom of the cylinder where the piston changes its direction of motion from the bottom to the top.

Stroke:

 
• **The distance travelled by the piston from TDC to BDC or BDC to TDC.**

Cycle:

 
• A set of operations performed in sequence by the motion of the piston in an engine to produce power.

Swept volume (VS):

 
• Displacement volume of a piston.

Clearance volume (VC):

 
• The volume of the space above the piston when it is at TDC.
 
• The space (volume) between the cylinder head and the piston head, when the piston is at TDC is called clearance volume.

Compression ratio (CR):

 
• The ratio of compression volumes before the stroke and after.
 
• CR = (V_S~+~V_C)/(V_C)

Where, VS = Swept volume, VC = Clearance volume, VS + VC = Total volume at BDC

Power:

 
• Power is the rate at which work is done at a specific time.

Horsepower (HP):

 
• It is the measurement of power in SAE. One hp is the power required to lift a load of 33000 lbs, through one foot in one minute or 4500 kg through one meter in one minute (in the metric system)

Thermal efficiency:

 
• It is the ratio of work output to the fuel energy burnt in the engine. This relationship is expressed in percentage.

Brake horsepower (BHP):

 
• It is the power output of an engine, available at the flywheel.

BHP~=~(2pi NT)/(4500) 

Where, N is the r.p.m of the crankshaft, and T is the torque produced.

Indicated horsepower (IHP):

 
• It is the power developed in the engine cylinder.

IHP~=~(PLAN)/(4500)~times~k 

Where Pm is the mean effective pressure in kg/cm2

 
• L is the length of the stroke in metres
 
• A is the area of the piston in cm2
 
• N is the No. of power strokes per minute,
 
• k is the No. of cylinders.

Frictional horsepower:

 
• It is the horsepower lost in the engine due to friction.

FHP = IHP – BHP

Mechanical efficiency:

 
• It is the ratio of power delivered (BHP) and the power available in the engine (IHP). It is expressed in percentage.

Volumetric efficiency:

 
• It is the ratio between the air drawn in the cylinder during the suction stroke and the volume of the cylinder.

Throw:

 
• It is the distance between the centre of the crank pin to the centre of the main journal. The piston stroke is double the throw.

Firing order:

 
• The firing order is the sequence in which the power stroke takes place in each cylinder in a multi-cylinder engine.

Exhaust Gas Recirculation (EGR) valve:

• Exhaust gas recirculation reduces the formation of NOX and engine knock control.

questions.question: The duration during which the inlet and exhaust valves remain open is called:

__Explanation:__
Valve timing:

 
• The opening and closing of the valves in an IC engine in relation to the movement of the piston and flywheel are called valve timing.
 
• Each manufacturer specifies the timings of the opening and closing of the valves as per the design of the engine to give the maximum output under all loads and speeds.
 
• The opening and closing of the valves exactly at TDC & BDC do not improve the volumetric efficiency of an engine.
 
• Burnt gases also are not driven out fully.
 
• Practically, the valves are arranged to open early and close late to fill the cylinder fully and to allow all burnt gases to escape from the cylinder.
 
• The valve timing is represented by a diagram drawn on the face of the flywheel in degrees of the crankshaft rotation.
 
• Valve timing (Jeep):
 
 
• The inlet valve opens 9 degrees before T.D.C.
 
• The inlet valve closes 50 degrees after B.D.C.
 
• The exhaust valve opens 47 degrees before B.D.C.
 
• The exhaust valve closes 12 degrees after T.D.C.
 
• Overlap period 21 degrees
 
 
 
• **Overlap period:**
 
 
• At the end of the exhaust stroke and the beginning of the suction stroke, both valves remain open for certain degrees. This period during which both the valves remain open is called the valve overlap.
 
 
 
• Valve timing varies from one make of engine to another Valves are exposed to various chemical, mechanical and thermal stresses during operation.

questions.question: In which type of EGR system, engine vacuum is used to operate the EGR valve?
questions.solution:
__**Explanation:**__

**Exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) system:**

 
• The purpose of an exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) system is to reduce NOx emissions that contribute to air pollution.
 
• Exhaust gas recirculation reduces the formation of NOX and engine knock control by re-circulating and allowing a small amount of exhaust gas into the intake air-fuel mixture on the intake manifold.
 
• EGR valve is connected between the exhaust port, or manifold and the intake system.
 
• If engine conditions are likely to produce oxides of nitrogen, the EGR valve opens, letting some gases is (only about 6 to 10% of the total) pass from the exhaust, into the intake system.
 
• During combustion, these exhaust gases absorb heat from the burning air and fuel.
 
• This lowers peak combustion temperatures (below 1500° C) to reduce the reaction between nitrogen and oxygen that forms NOx.
 
• Older EGR systems use a vacuum-regulated EGR valve while newer vehicles tend to have an electronic EGR valve to control exhaust gas recirculation.
 
• The EGR valve opens and closes the passage between the exhaust manifold and the intake manifold.
 
• **In vacuum controlled type of EGR system, an engine vacuum is used to operate the EGR valve.**
 
• The vacuum is removed by the EGR valve. Inside the vacuum-actuated EGR valve, there is a valve, diaphragm and spring.
 
• When the vacuum is applied to the diaphragm, it lifts the valve off its seat allowing exhaust gases into the intake air stream.
 
• When the vacuum is removed, the spring forces the diaphragm and valve downward closing the exhaust passage.

questions.question: Which of the following term is not related to battery?
questions.solution:
__**Explanation:**__

**Starting Motor:**

 
• The starter motor is fixed in the rear side of the engine, when the starter is switched on the starter motor’s pinion engages with the flywheel ring gear and rotates the flywheel.
 
• Once the engine starts running under its own power it attains a speed up to 4000 r.p.m. (depending upon the design).
 
• Since the flywheel ring-to-starter pinion ratio is very high, the starter pinion will rotate at a much higher speed than the engine.
 
• This speed will damage the starting motor by throwing the windings out of the armature slots and also the commutator segments due to centrifugal force.
 
• In order to prevent this it is necessary to disengage the starter pinion from the flywheel ring gear once the engine has started.
 
• To achieve this, three types of drive mechanisms are used:
 
 
• **Bendix drive**
 
• Over-running clutch drive
 
• Axial or sliding armature type and non-coaxial type
 
 

**Bendix drive:**

 
• This is the most commonly used mechanism.
 
• It consists of a pinion (1) which is mounted on a hollow sleeve.
 
• The pinion (1) has internal screw threads and is loosely fitted on the sleeve (2).
 
• The armature shaft (3) is supported by bearings at both ends.
 
• A Bendix drive spring (4) is provided to limit the turning of the sleeve on the armature shaft.
 
• An anti-drift spring (5) is provided to prevent the pinion from striking the flywheel (6).
 
• When the motor is switched on, the drive head rotates with the armature shaft (3).
 
• This motion is transmitted to the sleeve.
 
• The pinion (1) rotates along with the sleeve and travels forward to come in mesh with the flywheel ring gear (6).
 
• Now the engine’s crankshaft rotates and the engine is started.
 
• When the engine speed increases the pinion (1) is thrown back to its original position due to inertia.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a part of the turbocharger?
questions.solution:
__Explanation:__

**Muffler:**

 
• The muffler is normally located under the body of the vehicle and attached to the body or chassis with flexible mountings.
 
• In some trucks in which exhaust gases are directed upward, the muffler is mounted at the rear end of the cab and surrounded by a guard to prevent accidental touching.
 
• The muffler reduces the engine exhaust noise.
 
• It is a large cylindrical-shaped container, fitted with passages and chambers that absorb and dampen the noise of the exhaust gases.
 
• Often a small or pre-muffler is fitted in the exhaust system between the manifold and the main muffler.

Turbocharger:

 
• A turbocharger is mounted on the engine.
 
• Turbochargers are operated by exhaust gases.
 
• In a turbocharger, the **turbine wheel** housing is connected to the exhaust manifold.
 
• It increases the amount of air delivered to the engine cylinder, thereby more fuel can be burnt which increases engine power.
 
• Whenever the density of air is less than the density at atmospheric pressure, especially at higher altitudes, the turbocharger helps the engine to get sufficient air.
 
• An engine may have one or more turbochargers.
 
• A turbocharger is mounted on the exhaust manifold.
 
• It has a turbine wheel and a **compressor wheel** on the same shaft.
 
• Exhaust gases enter the turbine housing and rotate the turbine wheel.
 
• Compressor housing's inlet is connected to the air cleaner and compressed air is discharged to the inlet manifold through the outlet.

Hacksaw frame:

 
• A hacksaw frame is used along with a blade to cut metals of different sections and is specified by the type and maximum length of the blade that can be fixed.

The pitch of the blade:

 
• The distance between adjacent teeth is known as the ‘pitch’ of the blade.
 
• For cutting solid brass, the most suitable pitch of a hacksaw blade is 1.8 mm.
 
• The Hacksaw blade pitch to cut conduit and other thin tubes is 0.8 mm.
 
• For tool steel, high carbon, high-speed steel, etc. use a 1.4 mm pitch.

questions.question: What is the full form of RTV in the context of RTV sealer?
questions.solution:
__Explanation:__

RTV (Room temperature vulcanizing):

 
• RTV (Room temperature vulcanizing) is a type of silicone rubber that cures at room temperature.
 
• Room temperature vulcanizing (RTV) sealer is also called silicone sealer.
 
• It is available as a one-component product or mixed from two components (a base and a curative).
 
• It is used widely in the automotive industry as an adhesive/sealant, for example, to create gaskets in place.
 
• Applications include low-temperature over-moulding, making moulds for reproducing, and lens applications for some optically clear grades.
 
• RTV (Room Temperature Vulcanizing) Silicones can aggressively adhere to and readily release from most surfaces.
 
• They are also good for sealing, and filling spaces between surfaces, and gaskets.
 
• They adhere to rigid and flexible substrates including metal, glass, fibreglass (fibreglass-reinforced panels), cement, canvas, rubber, plastic, ceramics, and wood.
 
• Since they don′t run off, they′re good for vertical and overhead applications.
 
• One-Component RTVs require no mixing and vary in viscosity.
 
• They have high fuel and oil resistance, high tensile strength, excellent electrical insulation, and low volatility.
 
• Acetoxy Cure Silicone Sealants are excellent for use in construction and industrial applications due to their high and low-temperature stability.
 
• They cure by the reaction to moisture in the atmosphere.
 
• Alkoxy neutral Cure Silicones offer exceptional adhesion and are non-corrosive to most metals.
 
• They are typically used on substrates in contact with fuel, solvents, and chemicals.

questions.question: A centre punch is used for:
questions.solution:
__**Explanation:**__

**Punches:**

 
• Punches are used in order to make certain dimensional features of the layout permanent.
 
• There are two types of punches.
 
• They are centre punch and prick punch made of high carbon steel, hardened and ground.

**Centre Punch:**

 
• **A centre punch is used for point marking.**
 
• The angle of the point is 90° in a center punch.
 
• The punch mark made by this is wide and not very deep.
 
• This punch is used for locating the center of the holes.
 
• The wide punch mark gives good seating for starting the drill.

**Prick Punch/Dot punch:**

 
• The angle of the prick punch is 30° or 60°.
 
• The 30° point punch is used for making light punch marks needed to position dividers.
 
• The divider point will get proper seating in the punch mark.
 
• The 60° punch is used for marking witness marks and is called as dot punch.
